title: Bridging for a Retail Store Purchase in Liverpool
h1: Bridging for a Retail Store Purchase in Liverpool (search-result title; not confirmed as the on-page H1 element)
summary: Case study of a wealthy father seeking to finance two retail investment units in Liverpool as an investment for his daughters. The enquiry concerned two brand new Tesco Convenience stores, each with a fresh 15-year lease, priced at GBP 2.75 million per unit (GBP 5.5 million in total). The family are described as experienced commercial landlords who could have paid cash; the brief to Silver Oak Capital was therefore to source a UK high-street bank with a very low cost of funds, i.e. the cheapest rate available. Challenge: retail property lending has been difficult since Covid and high-street lenders have offered only conservative loan-to-value ratios on retail assets. Proposed structure: 55% LTV, 3.00% five-year fixed rate, 10-year interest-only term, 1.25% arrangement fee. The search results do not state the loan amount explicitly, the lender's name, the timeline, or whether the facility completed; they describe the structure as 'proposed'. Although titled 'Bridging', the terms described (5-year fix, 10-year interest-only) are those of a long-term commercial mortgage, an observation made by the search tool's summary rather than by the page itself. The firm's commercial-mortgage-broker page lists this case study among its examples.

sections.heading: The client and the enquiry
sections.content: A wealthy father wanted to finance two Liverpool retail units as an investment for his daughters. The enquiry concerned two retail assets: two brand new Tesco Convenience stores located in Liverpool. Each unit had a fresh 15-year lease and a price of GBP 2.75 million per unit. The family are described as experienced commercial landlords.

sections.heading: The brief
sections.content: The clients could pay cash; the firm's brief was to find a UK high-street bank with a very low cost of funds. Because the buyers had the funds, the broker aimed for the cheapest rate available.

sections.heading: The challenge
sections.content: Retail property lending has been hard since Covid. High-street lenders were cautious about retail assets and offered loans only at conservative loan-to-value levels.

sections.heading: The proposed structure
sections.content: 55% LTV; 3.00% five-year fixed rate; 10-year interest-only term; 1.25% arrangement fee. The search results describe this as the 'proposed' structure/solution and do not confirm completion, the lender's identity or the timeline.

sections.heading: Product-type observation (not from the page)
sections.content: The search tool's summary notes that although the page is titled 'Bridging', the terms described (five-year fix, ten-year interest-only) correspond to a long-term commercial mortgage rather than a short-term bridging loan. Silver Oak's commercial-mortgage-broker page lists this case study among its examples and states the firm arranges both short-term bridging and long-term commercial mortgages.
